Suppression versus secretion clearance

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient recovering from a respiratory infection asks whether an antitussive and an expectorant perform the same task. The clinician explains that one reduces cough signaling while the other is intended to aid mucus clearance. Which drug belongs to the latter category?

  1. Guaifenesin
  2. Benzonatate
  3. Codeine
  4. Dextromethorphan
  5. Hydrocodone
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Guaifenesin

Guaifenesin is an expectorant used to aid clearance of respiratory secretions.

Understanding the options

Guaifenesin
Guaifenesin is an expectorant used to aid clearance of respiratory secretions.
Benzonatate
Benzonatate suppresses peripheral cough signaling.
Codeine
Codeine is a centrally acting opioid antitussive.
Dextromethorphan
Dextromethorphan is a centrally acting nonopioid antitussive at therapeutic doses.
Hydrocodone
Hydrocodone is an opioid cough suppressant.
